data.narrative:
Planet Labs is a publicly listed Space & Aerospace company founded by Chris Boshuizen, William Marshall, and Robbie Schingler. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private frontier-tech companies in the same sector.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Across three same-sector, same-stage public comparables—Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M)—the median valuation is $2.9B. This wide range ($840M to $40.0B) reflects substantial dispersion in how the public market prices Space & Aerospace operators. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 27.4x across 6 tickers) cannot be applied, as Planet Labs' revenue is not on file. The target's current market valuation of $7.56B sits materially above the peer median, suggesting either execution premium or market optimism relative to the comp set.

The analysis supports a triangulated range of $2.5B to $3.3B (median $2.9B), grounded solely on peer-median methodology. Key uncertainties include the significant scatter in public Space & Aerospace valuations, absence of revenue data to apply multiple-based approaches, and the limited sample size (n=3). The gap between the peer median and current market price warrants investigation into company-specific growth drivers or market sentiment divergence.
